title: Chapter 45: The Effect of Her Lingering Scent
content:
Chapter 45:

The Effect of Her Lingering Scent

Kicking off the earth, he leaped forward.

Thick roots snake around his feet to get in the way, but he stomps them down in one fell swoop, crushing them underfoot as he powers through.

When traversing forests, mountains, or unpaved paths, it was actually a mistake to be cautious of your uncertain footing. When running along natural game trails, the right move was having the sheer decisiveness to push forward without hesitation, regardless of what lies underfoot; that was what carved a path.

Trusting in the sturdy soles of his shoes, he trampled over the piled-up branches, leaves, and moss, bounding forward once more.

His breathing was ragged. Sweat dripped down his forehead, threatening to sting his eyes, and he blinked painfully to clear a path for it to flow away.

He has neither the leeway nor the reason to look back. To begin with, the chances of actually escaping were virtually nil. Even now, the pursuers’ footsteps ran right alongside him, hounding him as if mocking his desperate flight.

Leaning his body forward to minimize wind resistance even a fraction, he sprinted with all his might.

His lungs burned, his whole body creaking as he gasped, desperate for oxygen. And then, to Subaru, who was clumsily opening and closing his mouth like a fish out of water,

“What a vulgar face… It really speaks to your upbringing.”

“——You, just remember this later, alright?!”

Regretting the wasted oxygen, Subaru shifts his grip around the girl in his arms—Ram—and holds her small frame closer.

The black haze likely connected to the Witch, and the “Great Natsuki Subaru Decoy Operation” that utilized it—had it been about ten minutes since it started?

Exactly as Subaru had planned, the battle with the gathering witchbeasts proved intensely fierce, until finally—left with no other options, the two had chosen to flee, bolting through the woods in defeat.

“I trusted you because you said you could fight, and now look at this!”

“Ram was fighting, actually. Her stamina just didn’t hold out as long as expected.”

“Didn’t you say something cool about crossing dangerous bridges?!”

“It was more dangerous than Ram imagined. We almost fell before we even started crossing.”

Ram’s responses to Subaru’s yelling were as unapologetically brazen as ever.

It was an unbelievable attitude for someone who couldn’t maintain her mana through repeated battles and was currently incapable of moving her limbs properly.

Drawn by the “Witch’s Lingering Scent” radiating from Subaru, the witchbeasts were being lured out without a hitch.

The sheer quantity of them completely shattered Subaru’s expectations; honestly, the spawn rate was so unmanageable that nothing but regret came to mind.

Utilizing wind magic, Ram had managed to dispatch a total of seventeen witchbeasts.

But right after taking care of them with such rapid efficiency, Ram suddenly lost all her strength and collapsed. Subaru, right beside her, was scared out of his wits, hurriedly throwing her over his shoulder and making a run for it—

“Which brings us to now—calling this ‘winging it’ would be an understatement.”

“Shut up, you’re the one being carried! And stop making me talk! I feel like I’m gonna bite my tongue… plus, I just, don’t, have the stamina…!”

He was a shut-in student yet held extraordinary scores in every athletic capability, but due to his nature of not going outside, only his lack of stamina was severe. When it came to long-distance running, his level was such that even finishing second-to-last in his school was within reach.

Yet, even with such pathetic stamina, having his life on the line meant he could still squeeze out a bit more. Though, his well of stamina running completely dry was only a matter of time.

The pursuing witchbeasts can probably tell that the fleeing Subaru was on the verge of collapsing.

As if savoring the process of their prey weakening, every time Subaru’s legs slowed down, they nipped at his heels to keep him in check, reigniting his fading instinct to flee.

“Barusu, right on your left. —Swing your sword and you’ll hit it.”

Turning her head in his arms, Ram gauged the shifting scenery and advised him of an easy target in range. Glancing over, Subaru spotted the snout of a witchbeast running alongside them from a position that completely underestimated him.

Aiming that way, he drew the one-handed sword from his hip in a single flash. Without missing his mark, the slash cleaved the arrogant witchbeast’s face cleanly in two, adding another fresh piece of fertilizer to the forest—was what did not happen.

As if losing patience with Subaru, who showed no sign of drawing his sword, anger flared in Ram’s eyes as she looked up at him from his chest. However, Subaru glared back with an equal amount of emotion,

“Why aren’t you drawing your sword?”

“I’ve got a whole person in my arms! How the hell am I supposed to swing a sword while running like this?! Even if I could, I’d miss, drop you, and trip, going out in one-two-three strikes, you idiot!”

Panting heavily at the put-off Ram, Subaru frantically pumped his legs, sweating profusely.

Despite Ram’s petite frame, the weight in his arms was still easily no less than forty kilograms. Just running for his life while carrying that much weight was a pretty stellar achievement in itself. Drawing a sword to fight on top of that was the kind of stunt you’d only see in a manga; Subaru simply couldn’t do it.

There was a limit to what an untrained ordinary student could do while carrying a girl. Naturally, that was why Subaru’s only choice was to grab her and run.

“It’s about time my hidden powers awakened—Ahhk!!”

His voice, eagerly awaiting the moment of his awakening, abruptly turned into a scream of agony as a sharp pain shot through his shoulder. Twisting around to look, he saw the fangs of a leaping witchbeast sunk deeply into his right shoulder. It was a strike from one that got bored of toying with them; his flesh was brutally gouged, and the pain of the fang’s tip grazing his collarbone made his throat tremble.

However,

“Carelessness is… your greatest enemy.”

Still cradled in his arms, Ram reached down to Subaru’s hip, drew his one-handed sword and executed a sharp, diagonal thrust.

The tip of the blade slips perfectly past the side of the witchbeast’s snout, destroying its brain and bursting out the back of its head. The strength behind the biting fangs instantly went slack, and Subaru’s running momentum shook the creature loose, sending it crashing to the dirt. Leaving the tumbling corpse behind, Subaru stared at the blade that had just flashed right past his face,

“Don’t do something so incredibly dangerous!”

“Ram just prevented the curses from stacking further. You should be thanking me. —Barusu, if an ulgarm bites you, you must kill it no matter what. Letting it escape only pushes your life further away.”

Deftly flicking the blood off the blade while still in his arms, Ram glared up at Subaru, delivering the warning. Feigning concentration on his running, Subaru refused to give her an answer.

Inside his closed mouth, he was fully aware that the roots of his teeth were trembling faintly.

He can’t tell if it was from the thrill of battle or out of sheer terror. No, that was a lie. He knew it was the latter, admitting it with a feeling akin to resignation.

He was terrified of the witchbeasts. Their fangs and claws terrified him beyond belief.

The sensation of the fangs that had just pierced his shoulder was shallow, but still sharp enough to trigger Subaru’s primal fears.

After all, he had been chewed to pieces, his entire body torn apart.

How could he ever forget that pain, that sense of loss, that pure despair?

Even with a sword in his hand, Subaru hadn’t driven his blade into a single witchbeast during his entire joint struggle alongside Ram. He has only been swinging it for crowd control, keeping them at bay so they can’t get close.

As a result, he forced the burden onto Ram, and was now forced to flee while carrying her exhausted body. Including the fact that he completely failed to imagine just how many witchbeasts would swarm them, it was all entirely Subaru’s own fault.

The wound on his shoulder ached. Blood trickled profusely from the tear in his clothes, leaving his right sleeve damp all the way down to his elbow. Feeling as though the strength was draining from his right arm, he readjusted his grip on Ram multiple times, desperately pushing forward. He just needs to change locations, even by a little bit.

“Ram!”

“On it.”

Replying curtly to his call, Ram’s eye dyed the color of blood.

She activated Clairvoyance at regular intervals, searching the surrounding area for any trace of Rem. While she does, Ram was left completely defenseless; protecting her during this time was Subaru’s job.

Darting his eyes around, he remained highly vigilant for any sign of a witchbeast lunging at them. Fortunately, perhaps deterred by the death of the previous one, none of them seemed to be making any blatantly aggressive moves. Instead, they just stalked him, maintaining a set distance to shadow his every move, waiting with bated breath for his stamina to run out.

Faced with this rather eerie silence, Subaru gulped, unable to fully shake a bad premonition.

From time to time, he swerved left and right to check them, altering his path to avoid any ambushes. But every time he repeated this, he lost track of the direction he was originally heading.

It had already been a long time since he lost his bearings regarding the village or the path deeper into the woods. Since Ram hasn’t said anything while using Clairvoyance, he just kept running, trusting that he had at least avoided running straight backward.

Abandoning these thoughts, the result of continuing to run with a completely empty mind was—

“Oh cra—!”

His reward came when the forest abruptly opened up and the ground beneath his feet vanished.

His legs kicked at empty air, and a weightless sensation assaulted him, feeling as though all his internal organs had been yanked up into his throat. A moment later, his heels scraped against a slope, his balance breaking as he transitioned into a slide.

It had scared the living daylights out of him, but it hadn’t exactly been a cliff drop.

More simply, they had stumbled into a basin sandwiched within the forest. He slid down the incline with the girl still in his arms, clumsily reaching the bottom while teetering on the edge of tumbling over. Just as he looked around, giving thanks for his good fortune in not completely wiping out, he realized his gratitude was extremely premature.

They’d fallen into a ravine in the woods, a V-shaped depression in the earth where the exit split to the left and right. However, the sounds of multiple witchbeast footsteps echoed from both paths. Simultaneously, there was the presence of the trailing witchbeasts sliding down the very slope Subaru just tumbled down.

“We’ve been had…!”

He shouldn’t have underestimated the witchbeasts as simple wild animals.

Despite sensing something akin to intelligence through their repeated clashes, Subaru had dismissed it because of the situation and their beastly appearance.

This allowed them to corral him along the path of their choosing, ultimately serving as the catalyst for luring him into a dead end with no escape.

In his arms, Ram remained oblivious to the severity of the situation, her vision still cast far away.

Tossing the responsibility of breaking out of this onto her, when she hasn’t even grasped the current reality, was impossible. Thus, overcoming this desperate predicament was the proof of trust she had placed entirely on Subaru’s shoulders.

“I just gotta do it…!”

A tendency to make snap decisions was one of the few redeeming qualities Subaru possesses.

Managing to tuck Ram into his left arm, he snatched the one-handed sword she was holding with his right. The wound on his right shoulder throbs dully, but it wasn’t the sort of injury that hindered his grip strength.

Breathing out heavily as presences closed in from three directions—left, right, and behind—Subaru raised the sword,

“Let’s go, raaaagh!”

Stabbing it into the slope right in front of him, he mobilizes every muscle in his lower body and right arm—and begins to conquer the incline ahead.

The method he chose was, once again, running away—the heroic act of breaking through one of the three paths to carve out a way forward wasn’t even worth considering. Given that he hadn’t been granted any combat hacks, it was a total unknown whether his blade would even reach the first beast.

Driving the blade in, finding purchase on the mossy slope with his soles, he uses his entire body to scale the steep hill. Tumbling down would mean game over, but standing around waiting for their end anywhere down there would yield the exact same result. In that case, unless he kicked the bucket after struggling to the very bitter end, none of this would have been worth it.

Twisting his body, he scraped the slope with everything from the elbow to the shoulder of his right arm, driving the blade in to gain every last drop of friction as he aimed for the top. Behind him in the basin, the witchbeasts that had intended to pincer them bumped their snouts together, looking up at his fleeing silhouette and letting out a chorus of roars.

But realizing his intentions now was far too late.

After plunging the blade into the dirt a good dozen times, Subaru and Ram reached the top of the slope. Leaning over the edge, he hooked his upper body over the lip and managed to haul them up,

“Yesssss! I did it! I actually freaking did it! Nice going, me! Good job, me! Mine venerable one-handed sword is chipped to hell and back, but… hu-OAH!”

Midst his endless self-praise, he immediately flung his body back down against the slope. An instant later, a tremendous gale swept right over his head, dragging a torrent of earth and sand with it—his nape, a second too slow to dodge, was gouged by the shockwave, bringing a sudden rush of searing heat and intense agony.

“——You bastard!”

Grimacing through the pain as he peeked over the edge again, a tiny silhouette stood in his line of sight far in the distance—there, making its fifth encounter with Subaru overall, was the puppy-like witchbeast.

Its four limbs were stretched out, belly to the ground in a crouched posture.

With its glowing red eyes locked squarely onto him, the creature swelled with an unquenchable hostility toward the prey it failed to finish off.

In other words, it was already preparing for a second shot.

“You gotta be kidding me, like I’m taking another one of those!”

As a torrent of mana began to interfere with nature, Subaru frantically scrambled over the top of the slope in a sheer panic. Putting off sheathing the sword or readjusting Ram in his arms, he scrambled out of the witchbeast’s field of vision—chasing after his fleeing back, the forest was trampled by a brutal horizontal mudslide.

Trees were mowed down and the very earth was torn up; he could feel the sheer, abnormal power right on his heels. There was no time to look back; his calf, trailing slightly behind in his flight, was ripped open by the shockwave’s aftermath, spraying blood.

“Dammit aaaaaall!”

He screamed, and jumped.

He threw himself to the right, leaping toward a completely different decline than before. Driven by the choice to outrun the landslide, and greeted by the baptism of yet another cliff face, Subaru reversed his grip on the sword and drove it back into the earth,

“Owowowowowow it hurts it hurts it hurts!”

His entire right half of his body scraping the earth, twisting the lodged sword to make it bite deeper, their skidding descent was subdued. Half-crying from the pain of all the fresh scrapes and cuts, Subaru looked up at the top of the cliff they had been falling from,

“Whoops.”

Carried by their own momentum, the bodies of witchbeasts unable to stop tumbled down the slope, and he deflected them as they fell.

Yelping like house pets, several witchbeasts plummeted straight down. Unlike the basin from earlier, the bottom of this slope was a ravine floor distinguished by jagged rocks. The falling witchbeasts were mercilessly embraced by the unyielding earth, silenced with the sickening crunch of shattering bones.

“We almost ended up saying our prayers too, but—”

“Barusu—! Ram found Rem!”

Ram lets out a cry of delight in his arms, her bloodshot eye returning to reality.

Then, following her joyful expression, she knitted her brows at the fact that their entire scenery was tilted at a harsh angle.

“Ram looks away for a little while, and what exactly is this situation?”

“Due to unavoidable circumstances we’re currently on a cliffhanger! Anyway, I’d rather hear about your results, mostly to distract myself from reality…”

Feeling the muscles in his arm shaking, Subaru shifted gears to distract himself with the good news. Without commenting on Subaru’s newfound injuries, Ram gave a small nod,

“Another field of vision caught Rem’s silhouette not too far from here. The timing was bad, so Ram couldn’t sync with Rem’s own sight, but she should be heading this way.”

“How do you know?”

“Because the vision Ram hijacked belonged to a ulgarm, and it ran into Rem while moving somewhere with a bunch of its pack. It got smashed to a pulp and the connection was severed.”

“Is that so…”

Subaru had no idea what kind of shock Ram experienced when a target she was sharing vision with died. But he imagined it was absolutely not a pleasant sight.

At any rate, confirming Rem’s safety was a stroke of luck. Just as he predicted, it seemed she was energetically playing hunter in the woods, which was perfectly fine.

“The problems are piling up way higher on our end, though… Rushing in thinking Rem was in danger, only to end up being the rescuers who need rescuing, no joke.”

“If we fall to the bottom of this cliff, even we’re going to be in danger, Barusu. Can you climb up?”

“I’ll manage with sheer guts. But the real problem is the witchbeasts chasing us up there…”

Wondering aloud what to do, he channeled strength back into the right arm holding them both. Leaning his weight onto the sword jammed diagonally into the dirt, he tried to shift into a slightly more comfortable posture,

““——Ah.””

Their voices overlap as a sharp, high-pitched screech of snapping steel rung out simultaneously.

The blade of the one-handed sword embedded in the cliff face snapped, leaving its front third buried in the slope. He frantically jabbed the warped blade back into the soil, but with the tip completely flat, the biting force was dreadfully weak, which simply meant—

“——The chances of those witchbeast bodies at the bottom acting as a cushion are…”

“The chances of us acting as a cushion for the witchbeasts falling after us is far higher.”

To Subaru’s words, spoken like a prayer to the heavens, Ram replied steeped in resignation. In that instant, the poorly lodged blade broke free from the slope, and their descent resumed.

Resigned to having his flesh scraped away, he pressed the entire right half of his body against the cliff face, but it wasn’t enough friction to support the weight of two people; utterly helpless, their bodies were violently launched toward the ravine floor.

“Daaahhhhh, craaaaap——!!”

“——This is going to cost you dearly, Barusu!!”

The sensation of falling headfirst brought back the memory of his past suicide leap, making his skin crawl and the hairs on his entire body stand on end. Yet, instinctively pulling Ram tighter into his arms to shield her from the impact proved he hadn’t given up on being a man just yet.

Feeling the brute-force embrace, Ram twisted slightly and thrusted her arm down toward the ground,

“——El Fula!!”

Her mana swelled alongside her shout, and the ground exactly where they were slated to impact exploded with a blast of wind.

The air pressure surging straight up from below caught Subaru’s falling body in an updraft, flipping their headfirst dive right-side up, and somewhat cushioning their terminal velocity.

This might work,

 he calculated amidst a world spinning half a rotation; pouring every ounce of strength into both legs, he braced for the incoming impact, clenching his jaw hard enough to crack his molars.

“Nghoooooooooooh, gaaahhhhh——I held on!!”

——He withstood it.

Shaking out his legs to placate the tremendous numbness shooting through them, Subaru looked up at the cliff they just plummeted from, utterly dumbfounded by the sheer height.

Over ten meters tall, it was roughly equivalent to the fourth floor of a school building. Thrown down onto solid earth from that height, it was honestly a miracle they had escaped with their lives.

“Seriously, praise Ram-sama and Buddha-sama for that timing. If it wasn’t for that wind magic, we’d be…”

Just as he tried to offer words of gratitude for cheating death, Subaru realized that Ram hasn’t twitched a single muscle in his arms. Looking closely, a trickle of blood ran from the nostril of the slumped Ram; her eyes closed, she took shallow breaths, doing nothing but groaning in pain.

“Huh? Hey, Ram? Crap, this is bad, hey.”

He gives her body a light shake and calls her name, but Ram doesn’t respond at all.

Her body had already been thoroughly exhausted from fighting the witchbeasts. Using magic to soften their fall just now was the final nail in the coffin, wearing her spirit down to the bone.

“Ah, dammit, my timing is the absolute worst.”

Cursing his own carelessness, Subaru hugged Ram even more protectively. Awkwardly shoving the broken half-sword back into its scabbard, he gazed upward.

At the top of the cliff, it seems the pursuing witchbeasts had begun searching for another route to detour around and track down Subaru and Ram, who took a brutal shortcut.

He wanted to put as much distance between them as possible while he still could, but—

“Even though I really don’t have time to waste here——?!”

Fleeing naturally cost time, and in a situation where that time loss tied directly to his life, holding back the urge to click his tongue at the fact that running was his only option was difficult. However, that bit of sentimentality was instantly snuffed out by a booming crash echoing from the top of the cliff.

“Hey, hey, you gotta be kidding me.”

Looking up directly overhead, a massive debris flow cascaded down the very slope Subaru just slid down—carrying atop it the puppy witchbeast, along with upwards of a dozen others.

Leaping back on instinct, he at least managed to avoid getting caught up in the mudslide itself.

But the moment the witchbeasts touched down on the same ground amidst the dirt and rocks, the advantage Subaru and Ram had risked their lives to create evaporated in an instant.

Added to that was the bonus that creating that brief window had sunk Ram’s consciousness to the bottom of the abyss, and Subaru’s already unreliable armament had become significantly more unreliable.

“Curse you, Witch-sama… Your perfume is way too strong.”

He offered his gratitude when the situation moved perfectly according to plan, and instantly flipped his opinion the moment he realized it was leading to his current downfall.

Dirty, as expected of Subaru, dirty,

 he thought, evaluating his own sheer pettiness, as he readied himself to flee once more, fully aware it would only delay the inevitable.

He was going to turn tail and bolt, praying the creatures were still underestimating them enough not to attack the very second they landed—

“Wait, huh?”

Right before he could break into a sprint, Subaru sensed something off and tilted his head.

The behavior of the witchbeasts sliding down was strange. He had been absolutely certain they were crouching atop the debris to pounce the exact second they landed, but—

“Uh, hey, I’m over here, you know?”

Just as Subaru’s dumbfounded voice indicated, the moment they touched down, the witchbeasts scattered in all directions, bolting away across the bottom of the cliff.

Scattering like baby spiders, their display was so deeply pathetic it instantly brought Subaru’s own desperate flight from moments ago to mind.

“What the hell is wrong with you guys—”

The tension of an imminent attack unraveled slightly, letting the question consume his thoughts.

An instant later, the answer exploded at the top of the cliff and rained down upon him.

“Eh?”

Looking overhead once again, bewilderment floated in Subaru’s eyes at the change atop the cliff—until he saw dark red chunks of meat raining down one after another before him, and finally understood.

——Far above, at the peak of the cliff, a single human silhouette appeared.

Swinging a blood-soaked iron ball wildly, it was a girl in a maid uniform, glaring down the cliff face with eyes utterly devoid of sanity.

The moment his eyes met that gaze utterly dominated by bloodlust, Subaru felt his back drenched in a cold sweat, seized by the absolute worst possible premonition.

Leaping immediately after, leaping from the high, high cliff down to this earth without a hint of difficulty, the “Oni” landed.

Surrounded by witchbeasts in a deep forest, facing off against an “Oni,” all while holding a girl he had to protect, with a broken sword in one hand, Subaru swallowed his breath, realizing he had finally reached the endgame.

“Still though, isn’t my position a tad too tragic?”

His plea reached no one, ignored in silence by the wind blowing through the forest.

Well now, this is what you call the real test——.

Reflected in the drawn blade of his one-handed sword, his own distorted profile looked terribly, terribly frail to Subaru.
